Fit the wrapped skew generalised normal by maximum likelihood (C back-end)

Source: R/wsgnstat.R
fit_wsgn_mle.Rd

Nelder-Mead over the identified parameters, with the wrapped log-likelihood evaluated in C. Standard errors, when requested, come from a parametric bootstrap, the observed information being unstable near the interior cusp the density develops as beta approaches one.

Usage

fit_wsgn_mle(theta, start = NULL, K = 50, B = 0)

Arguments

theta

numeric vector of angles in radians.

start

numeric starting value c(mu, beta, lam); default is the trigonometric-moment estimate.

K

truncation of the wrapping sum.

B

number of parametric-bootstrap replicates for standard errors; 0 skips them.

Value

a list with par, logLik, and (if B > 0) se.

Examples

set.seed(12)
truth <- c(mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)
th <- rwsgn(500, truth["mu"], truth["beta"], truth["lam"])
fit <- fit_wsgn_mle(th)
round(rbind(truth = truth, estimate = fit$par), 3)
#>             mu  beta   lam
#> truth    1.000 1.500 0.300
#> estimate 1.048 1.499 0.303
fit$logLik
#> [1] -663.4528
# \donttest{
## bootstrap standard errors refit the model once per replicate (a few seconds for B = 30)
fit_b <- fit_wsgn_mle(th, B = 30)
round(rbind(estimate = fit_b$par, se = fit_b$se), 3)
#>             mu  beta   lam
#> estimate 1.048 1.499 0.303
#> se       0.079 0.106 0.029
# }
